project_summary: A single-operator, point-in-time macro/FX data platform: three upstream sources (FRED/ALFRED, ECB SDW, Bundesbank) are fetched byte-faithfully into an append-only Postgres raw landing table, transformed by dbt into a bitemporal fact grain (series_id, obs_date, known_at) plus precomputed grain/transform marts, orchestrated by Dagster, and served through a read-only FastAPI layer (platform_reader) to Metabase, dbt docs, Elementary and a five-page Streamlit suite. Roughly 110 series and 0.75M fact rows are live, with the full Compose stack (12 services) running locally. The spec's build order is complete through M4 (Postgres/Compose, Dagster, dbt+Elementary, API, Metabase) plus substantial work beyond it (Data Ops selective refresh, Volatility Studio, a German-economy D3 dashboard, a country-scoring MVP), while M5 (unattended week), M7 (k3s/Tailscale) and M8 (CI/CD) are untouched.

what_works: Postgres warehouse bootstrap is real and verified: sql/001_init.sh creates raw/staging/intermediate/marts/meta/elementary schemas, the platform_writer/platform_reader roles and the append-only raw.source_fetch table; `make check` counts 6 schemas and passes at runtime.

Bitemporal fact grain and latest view are materialized: marts.fct_macro_observation (745,450 rows / 110 series) and marts.fct_macro_observation_latest (471,453 rows), with is_latest resolved in int_macro__observations_unioned.sql:33-37.

Dagster orchestrates a per-model asset graph (one asset per dbt model, ingest assets wired as deps of staging in orchestration/assets/dbt.py:21-52) plus a defined daily schedule (orchestration/schedules.py:12-17).

dbt is layered and tested: three per-source staging models, an intermediate union, 6 marts and a singular grain test; Elementary is installed with on-run-end artifact upload (dbt/dbt_project.yml:39-50).

FastAPI read layer works: /health, /ready, /v1/series, /v1/series/{id}, /v1/series/{id}/observations, /v1/observations, /v1/meta/freshness all return the {data,meta} envelope as platform_reader, and the 50-year range and 20-series bounds return HTTP 400 at runtime (verified by curl).

Owner-only /ops router is properly isolated at a non-/v1 prefix behind a constant-time X-Ops-Key check, and queues Dagster runs rather than writing the warehouse (api/ops.py:42-58, api/dagster_client.py).

Data Ops selective refresh is a genuine engineering highlight: a selector pre-flight via dbtRunner refuses an empty dbt selection, with the Elementary partial-select workaround documented (orchestration/ops.py:92-134, agents/notes.md:104-118).

Delivery surface beyond the spec exists and runs: Metabase, CloudBeaver, dbt docs, dbt deps report, Elementary report, launchpad and a 4-page Streamlit suite (Forecast Studio, Signal Lab, Volatility Studio, Data Ops) plus the German dashboard on :8084.
Precomputed analytics marts are populated and indexed: fct_macro_series_grains (806,952 rows), fct_macro_series_transforms (5,475,118 rows), fct_macro_series_period_metrics (806,952 rows).
what_is_incomplete: M5 has not started: the Dagster `instigators` table is empty (schedule never turned on), the runs table holds only 10 manually-triggered runs (6 SUCCESS / 4 FAILURE, 2026-09-05..09-17), and raw.source_fetch holds 275 fetch events for 110 series (~2.5 per series) instead of daily history.

The spec's four Dagster asset checks (freshness, volume, nulls, revision anomaly) are not implemented — there is no @asset_check anywhere; the 97 asset_check_executions rows all come from dbt tests via dagster-dbt.
No CI/CD: .github/ does not exist, so spec §16's ruff → mypy → pytest → dbt parse → dbt build → image build pipeline and the deploy workflow are absent.

make check is not the spec §22.2 gate: the Makefile has no lint/type/test/dbt-parse targets (ruff and mypy are not even dependencies), and every line ends in `|| echo "... FAIL"`, so `make check` printed FAIL-style output while still exiting 0.

Real FRED vintage history is not captured: ingest/fetch.py:49-54 calls the plain observations endpoint with no realtime_start/realtime_end, every observation in a fetch carries one request-scoped realtime_start (raw/fred/DEXUSEU/2026-09-06T12:50:15.866691Z.json shows 2026-08-31 for all 6,955 rows), and the warehouse holds at most 3 distinct known_at values for any series.

The spec §5 change-detection promise is unused: payload_sha256 is written and indexed but never read (referenced only in prose at dbt/models/staging/sources.yml:11), so every build re-explodes the entire raw history.
M7 and M8 are absent: no k8s/ manifests, no Tailscale/admin-plane separation, no cert-manager, no backup CronJob, no restore test.
Spec §12's repo layout is only partly delivered: no images/ split, no orchestration/resources/ or checks/, no scripts/smoke.sh, no CLAUDE.md, no docker-compose.override.yml.

The series catalog is maintained twice — ingest/config.py:81-216 (110 Series entries) and dbt/seeds/series_catalog.csv (110 rows) — and docs/api-calls.md:9-13 contradicts itself about which is authoritative.

Both analytics models and the liveability scorer are outside the warehouse/API: the country score runs in Python at page render (dashboard/liveability.py, scripts/liveability_model.py), there is no country mart and no POST /v1/score that spec §19 promises.
Observability beyond phase 0 is a proposal only (docs/observability-plan.md:3) and the spec §18 weekly digest does not exist; a 291-day-stale ECB HICP series sits in the warehouse unflagged.

Live data defects are visible and unguarded: ECB_HICP and ECB_HICP_CORE have not updated since 2025-12-01 (291 days), and one Bundesbank fetch (DE_TS_10Y) is recorded with HTTP 404 at 2026-09-17 15:24:13.
key_risks: Bitemporal integrity is the platform's central promise (spec §1.2, §6) but is currently unverifiable retroactively: with request-scoped known_at and no ALFRED backfill, 'what did we know on date X' can only be answered forward from the handful of fetches already stored.

Unbounded warehouse growth: staging reads every raw payload ever landed, so a daily schedule over 110 series would add a full history re-explosion per day on top of an already 5.47M-row full-refresh transform mart (spec §9's 'revisit when a build exceeds a minute' threshold is plausibly already crossed).

The daily schedule has never run unattended, so retries, timezone handling, credential expiry and idempotency are all untested — exactly the failure class spec §20 M5 exists to surface; there is no retry/backoff in the fetch clients at all.

Silent failures are systemic in the analytics layer: bare `except: pass` in lab.py/forecast.py/volatility.py and empty-DataFrame fallbacks in the Signal Lab loaders turn connection errors, failed diagnostics and failed CV folds into blank or NaN output indistinguishable from real results.

Documentation has drifted from the code in ways that mislead operators and agents: README claims a 'Postgres only' make up and '5 services' while Compose defines 13, docs/migration-plan.md still frames the retired DuckDB slice as current, index_100 is documented as series-inception but implemented per-grain, and the liveability docs disagree with the seed on country counts, child cost and the exit-tax rule.

Credential defaults are committed (ops_dev_key, writer_dev/reader_dev, Cloudbeaver123) and several are undocumented in .env.example, while invariant §22.5.5 forbids credentials outside .env/.env.example.

The public API is missing its stated defensive layer — no CORS allowlist, no Cache-Control, no page-size bound on observation endpoints, and a new Postgres connection per request — which is precisely the resource-abuse threat model spec §10 calls out.

initiatives.name: Engineering Foundations & Delivery Pipeline
initiatives.description: Restore the machine-checkable definition of done the spec's agentic build model depends on (M-1) and add the CI/CD pipeline that gates and ships changes (M8). Covers CLAUDE.md, a `make check` that actually fails, lint/type tooling, an endpoint smoke test, the image split the spec prescribes, CI for all three custom images, and the docs/repo-contract drift that currently misleads operators and agents.
initiatives.why: Spec §22.2 states that a green `make check` is the only acceptance signal an executor may claim, and §22.4/§22.5 require CLAUDE.md and the invariants list to be visible to every agent. Today `make check` always exits 0 (Makefile:15-21) and CLAUDE.md does not exist, so no automated verdict exists anywhere in the repo; with no .github/ there is also no CI, and no record of why the stack grew from the spec's 5 services to 12 (invariant §22.5.6).

initiatives.name: Data Contracts & Warehouse Integrity
initiatives.description: Close the gap between the spec's raw-landing and bitemporal contracts and what the code actually delivers, and keep the warehouse rebuildable and affordable as it grows. Covers real FRED/ALFRED vintages, the spec §6 no-change rule for ECB/Bundesbank, payload_sha256 change detection, bounded staging fan-out, incremental/partitioned marts, a single authoritative series catalog, the spec §8 asset checks, and the dbt tests that make mart semantics trustworthy.
initiatives.why: The platform's reason to exist is point-in-time correctness ('vintages are preserved', spec §1.2), yet known_at is request-scoped for FRED and fetch-dated for ECB/Bundesbank, the sha256 skip mechanism is unused, and staging re-reads all history on every build — already 745k fact rows and 5.47M transform rows. Meanwhile the catalog is hand-maintained in two places and the four spec §8 asset checks do not exist, so a 291-day-stale ECB series produced no signal.
module_names: Series Catalog Single Source of Truth

initiatives.name: Data Serving & Analytics APIs
initiatives.description: Make the read layer honour the full spec §10 contract (CORS allowlist, cache headers, enforced query bounds, pooled connections, honest warehouse_build provenance) and then expose the platform's second analytics payload — country scoring and liveability — through a warehouse mart and a POST /v1/score endpoint as spec §19 anticipates.
initiatives.why: The API already returns the correct envelope and enforces two of the three bounds, so this is finishing a contract rather than designing one: runtime probes show no Cache-Control header, a 405 on CORS preflight, a silently ignored page-size parameter, and one new psycopg connection per request. Country scoring currently runs in Streamlit at render time from a Python-only seed, which means the platform's most opinionated output is neither reproducible nor versioned in the warehouse.

initiatives.name: Unattended Operations & Reliability
initiatives.description: Turn the platform from something a human triggers into something that runs and reports itself: enable and prove the daily schedule (M5), make ingest resilient and observable, ret rid of the Dagster-bypassing legacy pipeline script, and add the backup/restore and alerting loop the spec requires before the box holds data worth losing (spec §17, §18).
initiatives.why: The schedule is defined (orchestration/schedules.py:12-17) but has never been enabled — the Dagster instigators table is empty and all 10 recorded runs were manual — so the spec's own M5 criterion (seven consecutive green runs) has not been attempted and every assumption about credentials, retries, timezones and idempotency remains untested. Nothing dumps Postgres, adjacent state (Metabase H2, CloudBeaver) is outside any backup scope, and the spec's weekly digest tripwire does not exist.

initiatives.name: Production Deployment on k3s
initiatives.description: Execute the Compose-first, k3s-second half of the plan: author the manifests, probes and resource limits, build multi-arch images and publish them with immutable SHA tags, and enforce the two-plane access model so exactly one public hostname exists (api.) while Dagster, Metabase and the reports stay on the tailnet.
initiatives.why: Spec §1.5 and §20 M7 deliberately defer the cluster until the pipeline has run unattended locally for a week, so this initiative is gated on Unattended Operations by design. Nothing of it exists yet (no k8s/, no .github/), and §15a warns that the window between 'the box is on the internet' and 'access control is configured' is the one that gets exploited — Tailscale must be installed before the first Ingress.

initiatives.name: Analytics Delivery & Research Surface
initiatives.description: Harden the research-facing surface that has grown well past the spec: give the Streamlit suite and the German dashboard shared, cached, pooled data access; replace silent exception swallowing with visible failures; add the unit tests the analytics modules have never had; and consolidate the artefacts (reference prototypes, DuckDB leftovers, duplicated liveability models) that make the repo ambiguous about what is canonical.
initiatives.why: Roughly 4,400 lines of analytics code (lab.py, volatility.py, forecast.py, liveability.py, the four pages, germany/main.py) have zero test coverage while carrying bare `except: pass` blocks and magic constants, and durable README/spec claims about them are already false (the filtered slice does not feed the Decomposition tab; scikit-learn ships but is never imported; Signal Lab never reads the period-metrics mart built for it). work_items.name: Commit CLAUDE.md as the binding agent contract at repo root
work_items.description_markdown:
Spec §22.2 requires a root `CLAUDE.md` loaded into every agent's context, containing: a pointer to `platform-spec.md` as the authoritative design document, the five design principles from §1 verbatim, the seven invariants from §22.5 verbatim, the commands (`make up`, `make check`, `make smoke`, how to reach Dagster locally), environment facts (macOS, arm64, Docker Desktop, Compose not k3s until M7), and the rule that no agent edits `sql/001_init.sh` or the bitemporal grain without an explicit human decision.

**Acceptance criteria**
- `CLAUDE.md` exists at repo root and contains all five sections above.
- The invariants are quoted verbatim, including §22.5.6 (no new Compose service without a decision).
- `agents/notes.md` is referenced for gotchas rather than duplicated.

Note: `README.md:9-10` currently points agents at `docs/migration-plan.md` and `agents/notes.md` only, and `agents/notes.md:45-47` records that two specs once existed — the contract file is the missing piece.
work_items.evidence: platform-spec.md §22.2 (lines 865-873), §22.5 (925-941); `ls CLAUDE.md` -> No such file or directory; README.md:9-10

work_items.name: Make `make check` a real gate with lint, type, test and dbt-parse targets
work_items.description_markdown:
The current `check` target is a set of Docker health probes, not the spec §22.2 chain, and it cannot fail: every recipe line ends in `|| echo "... FAIL"`, so make sees a successful command and exits 0. Running `make check` on a fully healthy stack printed all five OK lines and `echo $?` returned 0 — the reversed experiment (a stopped service) would also exit 0, which destroys the only acceptance signal spec §22.2 permits an executor to claim.

**Acceptance criteria**
- `make check` depends on `lint type test dbt-parse` and exits non-zero if any of them fails.
- `lint` = `ruff check . && ruff format --check .`; `type` = `mypy orchestration api`; `test` = `pytest -q`; `dbt-parse` = `cd dbt && dbt parse`.
- The existing container-health probes move to a separate `check-stack` target that also exits non-zero and additionally covers metabase, elementary-report, dbt-deps-report, launchpad, cloudbeaver and germany-dashboard.
- `make ingest` and `make dbt` exist per spec §12.
- Demonstrate both directions: green tree -> 0; deliberately broken lint -> non-zero.
work_items.evidence: Makefile:1 (targets are only up/down/build/psql/check/reset), Makefile:15-21 (each probe ends `|| echo "... FAIL"`); observed `make check; echo $?` -> `exit=0` with all OK; platform-spec.md:852-864

work_items.name: Add ruff and mypy with repo configuration and dev dependencies
work_items.description_markdown:
`pyproject.toml`'s dev dependency group contains only pytest, and there is no `[tool.ruff]` or `[tool.mypy]` section, so spec §22.2's `lint`/`type` targets cannot exist. This also blocks spec §16's CI first two steps.

**Acceptance criteria**
- `ruff` and `mypy` added to `[dependency-groups] dev` and to `uv.lock`.
- `[tool.ruff]` and `[tool.mypy]` configured in `pyproject.toml` with a line length matching the existing code style.
- `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .` and `mypy orchestration api ingest` all exit 0 on the current tree (fix or explicitly noqa findings rather than narrowing the target set silently).
- Document the commands in `CLAUDE.md`.
work_items.evidence: pyproject.toml:23-26 (dev group = pytest only); no `[tool.ruff]`/`[tool.mypy]` anywhere; platform-spec.md:855-856

work_items.name: Add scripts/smoke.sh asserting 200/400 on every documented endpoint
work_items.description_markdown:
Spec §22.2 names `smoke: ./scripts/smoke.sh  # curl every endpoint, assert 200/400` as part of the M-1 precondition, and §22.4 says `DONE WHEN` must be an executable command. The script does not exist, so there is no endpoint-level verdict at all.

**Acceptance criteria**
- The script curls and asserts: `/health` 200, `/ready` 200, `/v1/series` 200, `/v1/series/{known}` 200, `/v1/series/{unknown}` 404, `/v1/series/{known}/observations` 200, `/v1/observations` 200, `/v1/meta/freshness` 200, a >50-year range 400, >20 series_ids 400, and (once bound enforcement lands) an over-max page size 400.
- Exit code is 0 only when every assertion passes; failures print the offending request and status.
- Wired into `make check` and into CI.

It must exercise the same surface `README.md:71-87` documents.
work_items.evidence: platform-spec.md:859; `ls scripts/smoke.sh` -> No such file or directory; README.md:71-87; api/main.py:154-249

work_items.name: Add pytest coverage for the API layer (bounds, envelope, 404 paths)
work_items.description_markdown:
`tests/` contains only `test_parse.py` and `test_liveability_model.py`; nothing tests the FastAPI layer, whose bounds and envelope are the contract the spec cares about most. The bound logic (`_range_check`, `MAX_SERIES_IDS`, `MAX_PAGE_SIZE`) is pure and trivially testable with `fastapi.testclient`.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Tests cover: `from > to` -> 400; range > 50 years -> 400; `series_ids` with 21 ids -> 400; empty `series_ids` -> 400; unknown series -> 404; `/health` without DB; `/ready` reports 503 when the DB is unreachable.
- Envelope shape asserted for each `/v1` route (keys `data`, `meta`; meta contains `row_count`, `generated_at`, `warehouse_build`).
- Tests run against a stubbed/connection-injected DB so they pass in CI without Compose.
work_items.evidence: tests/ = test_parse.py + test_liveability_model.py only; api/main.py:118-122, 174, 226-235; platform-spec.md:401-410

work_items.name: Split the single image into platform-dagster and platform-api as the spec prescribes
work_items.description_markdown:
Spec §2 states there are exactly two custom images (`platform-dagster`, `platform-api`) and §12 places them at `images/dagster/Dockerfile` and `images/api/Dockerfile`. Today one root `Dockerfile` is built by six services (dagster-webserver, dagster-daemon, api, elementary-report, dbt-deps-report, dbt-docs), and the file itself acknowledges the deviation.

**Acceptance criteria**
- `images/dagster/Dockerfile` carries dbt + dagster + elementary; `images/api/Dockerfile` carries FastAPI/psycopg only and drops the dbt/Dagster dependency tree.
- `docker-compose.yml` references the correct Dockerfile per service; the api image must not contain dbt.
- Both images build for `linux/arm64`.
- Image sizes recorded before/after in the PR description; `docker compose up` still yields a healthy stack.
work_items.evidence: Dockerfile:1-3 (comment acknowledging the spec split); docker-compose.yml:22, 48, 61, 153, 166, 179 (same root Dockerfile); platform-spec.md:43-54, 469-471

work_items.name: Record decision records for the services added beyond the spec's five-service inventory
work_items.description_markdown:
Spec §2 inventories five services and invariant §22.5.6 forbids adding a service to `docker-compose.yml` without an explicit decision, because that is how a five-container stack becomes eleven. The stack now defines 12 services: the seven additions are `dashboard` (Streamlit), `germany-dashboard`, `cloudbeaver`, `launchpad`, `elementary-report`, `dbt-deps-report` and `dbt-docs`. Every one of them is a reasonable addition, but none has a recorded decision, and two of them (`elementary-report`, `dbt-deps-report`) exist only to serve generated artefacts on a timer.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A short ADR per added service (or one consolidated record) stating purpose, why it is not a spec violation, resource cost on the laptop, and its production disposition (k8s Deployment, static file, or not deployed).
- Records note that `elementary-report` as a long-lived service contradicts spec §9 and link the remediation ticket.
- Invariant §22.5.6 restated so future agents have a place to record the decision.
work_items.evidence: docker-compose.yml:81-110, 129-144, 146-183 vs platform-spec.md:43-49 and invariant §22.5.6 (line 934); docs/observability-plan.md:74 (port-collision list implies an unplanned stack)

work_items.name: Refresh docs/migration-plan.md so it describes the shipped Postgres stack

work_items.name: Capture real FRED revision history through ALFRED real-time parameters
work_items.description_markdown:
The spec chose FRED as source #1 precisely because its vintage support lets the bitemporal model be built against real revision history (spec §3), and the fact grain is `(series_id, obs_date, known_at)` (spec §6). But `fetch_fred` requests the plain observations endpoint with only `series_id`, `api_key`, `file_type` and `observation_start`; it never sends `realtime_start`/`realtime_end`. FRED therefore labels every observation in a response with one request-scoped realtime date: `raw/fred/DEXUSEU/2026-09-06T12:50:15.866691Z.json` carries `realtime_start = 2026-08-31` on all 6,955 rows, and a warehouse query shows at most 3 distinct `known_at` values for any series (minimum 1). `docs/migration-plan.md:89-92` flagged exactly this and it is still open.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Fetch uses ALFRED real-time semantics (`realtime_start`/`realtime_end`, or the vintage/release endpoints) so a historical vintage can be retrieved deliberately.
- A backfill job populates revision history for at least the daily FRED series, with `pdf`/`realtime` semantics recorded per row.
- `known_at` values are distinct per genuine revision rather than uniform across a fetch.
- A test proves an as-of query for a historical date returns the value known then, distinct from today's value where a revision exists.
- Landed rows remain byte-faithful in `payload_raw` and the change is reflected in `docs/api-calls.md`'s FRED section, which currently documents a response shape with no realtime fields at all.

work_items.name: Apply the spec §6 insert-only-on-change rule to ECB and Bundesbank vintages
work_items.description_markdown:
Spec §6 prescribes the exact approximation for providers without vintages: set `known_at = fetched_at::date` and 'only insert a new row when the value differs from the last known one'. The staging models do the first half and skip the second, so every daily fetch re-stamps the entire history with a new `known_at` even when nothing changed. This fabricates revision history out of fetch events and is the main driver of fact-table growth.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Staging (or an intermediate no-change filter) emits an ECB/Bundesbank row only when the value differs from the previously known value for that `(series_id, obs_date)`, or when no prior row exists.
- A repeated fetch with identical bytes produces zero new fact rows for those sources (verify by running the pipeline twice and diffing `count(*)` in `marts.fct_macro_observation`).
- A test covers both directions: unchanged payload -> no new vintage; changed value -> exactly one new vintage dated `fetched_at::date`.
- FRED is explicitly exempt from the rule, since it has genuine vintages.

work_items.name: Use payload_sha256 to skip downstream work for byte-identical fetches
work_items.description_markdown:
Spec §5 introduces `payload_sha256` specifically to 'enable skipping downstream work when a fetch is byte-identical to the previous one — a cheap and reliable change-detection mechanism', and `sql/001_init.sh:50-51` even creates an index on it. The column is written by `ingest/load.py` and then never read: the only other reference in the dbt tree is a prose description in `sources.yml:11`. Every build therefore re-processes unchanged payloads.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Staging (or a dbt incremental predicate) selects only fetch events whose `payload_sha256` differs from the previous fetch for that `(source, resource)`, while still retaining the raw rows for audit.
- A second consecutive pipeline run with unchanged upstream data performs no mart rewrite for those series and the build time is measurably lower.
- The `raw.source_fetch` index on `payload_sha256` is used by the query (verify with EXPLAIN).
- Failed fetches (null payload) are handled explicitly and never treated as 'unchanged'.

work_items.name: Bound the staging fan-out to the newest payload per (source, resource)
work_items.description_markdown:
Each staging model reads every fetch event ever landed (`where source = 'fred' and payload is not null`) and explodes its full observation array, so the intermediate union scales with (number of fetches) x (observations per fetch) rather than with the data itself. With 275 raw fetch events for 110 series the warehouse already holds 745,450 fact rows and 471,453 latest rows; a daily schedule would add a complete history re-explosion per day on top of that, and every upstream byte of history is a full-history payload.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Staging selects only the fetch events needed to reconstruct current state — at minimum the newest payload per `(source, resource)`, plus older payloads only when a genuine vintage differs.
- Row counts are documented with a ceiling as an explicit test: a repeated run must not multiply `marts.fct_macro_observation` by the number of fetches.
- `int_macro__observations_unioned.sql`'s dedup remains necessary for genuine vintages and is not relied on to absorb redundant re-statement of unchanged history.
- Before/after row counts and build times recorded in the PR.

work_items.name: Make the yield-curve endpoint degrade gracefully when a BBSIS tenor is missing
work_items.description_markdown:
The dashboard advertises a complete 0.5-30Y curve with `interpolated_tenors: 0`, built from 31 Bundesbank BBSIS series fetched individually. A recorded failure shows how fragile that is: `raw.source_fetch` contains a null-payload row for `DE_TS_10Y` with HTTP 404 at 2026-09-17 15:24:13, so a single upstream hiccup can leave a hole in the curve. Nothing in the endpoint contract says what the consumer should render in that case.

**Acceptance criteria**
- The endpoint reports, per tenor, whether a value is present and when it was observed, so the frontend can render a gap rather than a straight-line interpolation that pretends to be data.
- `interpolated_tenors` reflects reality; if a tenor is carried forward or interpolated, it is counted and labelled.
- A test with a fixture missing one tenor asserts the response marks the gap and does not silently shift the curve.
- The recorded 404 is investigated: confirm whether the BBSIS key for the 10Y residual maturity is correct and whether ingestion has since recovered.

work_items.name: Bound the raw landing contract: append-only, sha256-indexed, failed fetches recorded
work_items.description_markdown:
Delivered and verified. `raw.source_fetch` exists with the spec §5 column set, a `(source, resource, fetched_at DESC)` index, a `payload_sha256` index, and no update/delete path in the codebase. `ingest/load.py` inserts one row per fetch event with parsed `payload`, byte-faithful `payload_raw`, the digest and `dagster_run_id`, and records a failed fetch as a null-payload row with its HTTP status rather than raising. work_items.name: Bitemporal fact grain with is_latest and a latest view
work_items.description_markdown:
Delivered and verified. The three staging models unpack the JSON payloads to typed `(series_id, obs_date, known_at, value, fetched_at)`; `int_macro__observations_unioned.sql` unions them, deduplicates to the grain `(series_id, obs_date, known_at]` keeping the newest `fetched_at`, drops null values, and computes `is_latest` per `(series_id, obs_date)`. `marts.fct_macro_observation` carries a surrogate key over the grain (unique-tested) and `marts.fct_macro_observation_latest` filters `is_latest`. Live: 745,450 fact rows and 471,453 latest rows across 110 series.

The structural decision is therefore in place; the open work is fidelity of `known_at` itself (ALFRED, the no-change rule, the type decision) and the row-growth consequences of restating history on every fetch.

work_items.name: Enforce the 50-year range and 20-series query bounds with HTTP 400
work_items.description_markdown:
Delivered and verified at runtime. `api/main.py` defines `MAX_SERIES_IDS = 20` and `MAX_RANGE_DAYS = 50 * 365`, `_range_check` rejects `from > to` and any range beyond the limit, and the multi-series route rejects more than 20 ids and an empty list — all with 400 and a message naming the limit, in Pydantic/routing rather than in SQL. work_items.name: Owner-only /ops trigger router with constant-time key check and dbt selector pre-flight
work_items.description_markdown:
Delivered and verified. Spec §10's owner-only rule is implemented exactly: the router lives at `/ops` (never under `/v1`), every route depends on `require_key`, the key is compared with `secrets.compare_digest`, and an unset `OPS_API_KEY` fails closed with 503 rather than opening the router. The API writes no warehouse data — it queues Dagster runs over GraphQL and reports them, keeping Dagster the single orchestrator. The refreshing path also solves a real trap documented in `agents/notes.md`: `dbt build --select <typo>` exits 0 having transformed nothing, so `_assert_selection_matches` pre-flights the selector through dbt's own runner and refuses to run an empty selection.

Follow-ups tracked separately: the router imports the ingest registry instead of reading `marts.dim_series`, and it blanks the `unit` field it already selects.
